toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Compared where the days are lost, step by step and by loan type, against the dates of each change. Then read the policy wording and the withdrawal reasons.
output.brief:
Nearly all the slowdown is in one step: collateral valuation on property-secured loans. It took 1.6 days in March and 1.7 in April, then 7.6 in June and 8.4 in August. Other steps barely moved; unsecured loans are back to normal. The jump follows the 1 May credit policy refresh, which lowered the loan size needing a full inspection appraisal from $500k to $150k; nobody assessed the processing-time effect. The valuation firm's April renewal brought no slowdown, Corvane caused only a short April bump, new-hire branches match the others, and Credit Hub underwriting is flat. I'm about 85–90% sure; I haven't seen the valuation firm's own turnaround figures.

Withdrawals are less clear: 32 of 73 recent closures are new automatic closures of files inactive for 30 days, which the old system never counted, so the rise may be mostly a counting change.

Next: don't withhold Corvane's payment or put new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay and the audit rationale (desktop valuations overstated by a median 12%) to the credit risk committee to decide on the threshold. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard, report automatic closures separately, and hold off on fee rebates.
